Subject: SOC 2 period question — inclusive end date and point-in-time evidence

Hi Camila,

Quick question as we prepare the testing plan for Brightwater's SOC 2 review: your report lists the coverage as "through June 30, 2026 (inclusive)". For our testers who will pull point-in-time samples and log extracts, can you confirm how Redwood defines the end-of-day on June 30? Specifically:

- Do you treat "inclusive" as up to 23:59:59 in Redwood's control-owner local time by default, or do you normalize to UTC (i.e., 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z)?
- If samples are taken at 00:00:00 on 2026-06-30 (UTC), will those records be considered inside the period or would they be treated as earlier in the day depending on timezone conversion?
- We also want to confirm whether Redwood will provide any bridge letter for material events occurring on 2026-07-01 that affect controls started within the reporting period.

If you can confirm the timezone convention and an example of how you tie logs to the "June 30 inclusive" cutoff (a couple of timestamp examples would be perfect), that will speed our test planning.

Thanks — we aim to finalize the sample list by Friday.

Best,
Lena

Subject: RE: SOC 2 period question — inclusive end date and point-in-time evidence

Hi all — thanks for bringing this up. To make the audit testing deterministic we provide the following guidance for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II reports and point-in-time evidence:  

1) Cutoff definition (Redwood default): the reporting period is inclusive through 23:59:59 on the last calendar date stated in the report using the control-owner's local timezone. For platform-wide controls maintained by Redwood, the control-owner timezone is America/Los_Angeles (PDT/PST as applicable).

2) How to interpret timestamp samples: when auditors request "point-in-time" evidence for 2026-06-30, any record with a timestamp >= 2026-06-30T00:00:00 (America/Los_Angeles) and <= 2026-06-30T23:59:59 (America/Los_Angeles) is considered within the period. If you prefer UTC-normalized timestamps, convert the above range to UTC and we'll provide extracts with both original and UTC fields to make tie-outs straightforward (we include timezone offsets in all log lines).

3) Examples (included in attached csv):
- Redwood local: 2026-06-30T00:00:00-07:00 through 2026-06-30T23:59:59-07:00
- UTC equivalent: 2026-06-30T07:00:00Z through 2026-07-01T06:59:59Z (note the calendar date moves depending on tz conversion).

4) Point-in-time extraction best practices:
- We recommend auditors extract both the original log timestamp and an ISO8601 UTC-normalized field.
- For database snapshots, provide the dump creation timestamp and the DB server timezone; we will include server timezone metadata.
- For KV cache snapshots (volatile state), provide the API request and response timestamps alongside the cache TTL and generation timestamp.

5) Bridge letters: Redwood is able to provide a bridge letter for discrete events occurring after the reporting period that materially affect controls. To draft one we need: (a) the exact event date/time; (b) a short description of the event & impact; and (c) supporting evidence. We have a bridge-letter template that we can populate and sign.

I'll attach the tie-out instructions and some timestamp examples to this thread. Camila / Rishi: please add any controls-specific notes if an auditor requests a different timezone convention.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
